logline: A hitchhiker refuses to obey an unseen rule, and the highway turns against her.
story: I slam the rear window, truck siren erupting through my quiet drive. The glass shatters, I clutch cold shards, pressing them against my palm, seeking silence. A rusted sign reads Do Not Stop, and highway lights dim progressively. I recall the rule: stopping amplifies the echo louder than one’s breath. I sever the hitchhiker’s hand from the seat, and the road’s hum intensifies. Car headlights flicker; a cracked mirror shows my reflection moving then vanishing. The hitchhiker’s face materializes in the rearview, eyes hollow, lips murmuring numbers. I pivot, and the road ahead transforms into a wall of faded photographs, each blinking. Numbers reverberate, photographs seep into night, assembling a staircase of darkness. The rule never meant to look; observation unravels the paint consuming the scene. Paint curls around my hands, world folds, a name slides in darkness unseen. Silence after the stop, the world withdraws, and my reflected breath disappears.
